description: Count its violet eyes and you have already lost it. The smoke it trails is the only warning anyone gets.
lore: Count the eyes. There are four, two low and wide and two smaller up on the brow, and by the time you have counted them you are inside the distance it needs — the joke every teller makes, and the reason the count is the first thing said about it. What the tellers leave out is that it used to have two. The oldest heads at the fires out on the grass learned it with two, and will admit as much if you are patient.

Nothing about a cat in the dark survives being told except eyes. Ask anyone who has met one what they saw and you get eyes, then a smell, then how fast it was, in that order, every time. That is most of what this one is now: the parts that get told, kept hard, the rest let go. The smoke off its back is the same business, the smear of dark that follows anything you only half saw. It has been thinning for centuries and thickening exactly where people hold it, and the two have met in the middle to make something that is nearly all warning and hardly any animal. The copses it used to work are gone — nobody was telling about them, and a Turn took the rest — so it hunts open grass now, in plain sight, and it is no easier to see. Nobody ever lost one of these behind cover. You lose it because the only parts anybody can hold are the eyes and the smoke, and neither of those is where the animal is. It has nowhere to hide out here and has never once needed anywhere.

[[characters/cfe826c1|Jehanne]] has had the argument three times and never lost it. The proposal is always identical: stop telling it. Leave it out of the round, let it go the rest of the way, and the open country is quiet inside a generation. She keeps a rota for a faith she stopped believing in years ago and she will not do this. A fire that decides what it is prepared to remember, she said once and has not said since, has stopped being a fire and become a committee. So the telling goes on, and the animal keeps getting better at being one.
gm_notes: Come, and being redrawn: it fell as an ordinary night cat, thinned, and the Keeping filled the gaps with the only parts anyone ever remembers of a cat in the dark, so it grew eyes. Art shows four; the count rising over time is the hook and the description's joke. The turn is Jehanne's, and it is a genuine moral bind — the one way to make the open country safe is to let a creature be forgotten on purpose, and the teller who no longer believes is the one who refuses. Do not resolve it. Ground is data-driven: maps2 moved it to grass in MONSTER_HABITAT and the text followed it out of the black wood, which cost the record nothing and gained it something — a creature whose concealment was never physical is exactly the one that loses nothing in the open.
